description:
I am a Computer Science student from Pakistan, passionate about technology, innovation, and problem-solving. I am interested in web development, AI, and using NASA data to solve real-world challenges. I am working on a project focused on climate-smart agriculture and helping farmers adapt to changing environmental conditions.

I am looking for motivated teammates with skills in web development, UI/UX design, data analysis, agriculture, and scientific research. Let's build something impactful!
summary:
FIELDSHIFT AI is a Flutter decision-support app that turns NASA Earth observation data into practical crop rotation advice for climate-resilient farms. It compares four rotation strategies side by side, including a conventional monoculture baseline, and explains each one with NASA evidence, information gaps and local risks. An interactive map overlays NASA GIBS imagery (MODIS, SMAP, NDVI, land surface temperature) and highlights field vulnerability zones for erosion, water stress, frost and bare-ground carbon loss. A what-if simulator stress-tests farms against temperature and rainfall changes. The app also offers Simple Farmer and Specialist views, English, Urdu and Hindi, an offline fallback, and CSV and advisory report export.

It addresses the "Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge by making NASA POWER, SMAP, MODIS, GRACE, ECOSTRESS, GPM IMERG and SRTM data usable by farmers and extension officers. It matters because heat, erratic rain and groundwater depletion threaten food security, and FIELDSHIFT AI supports, rather than replaces, local farmer expertise.
details: WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS FIELDSHIFT AI is a Flutter decision-support app that turns NASA Earth observation data into practical crop rotation advice for farmers and extension officers. It compares four strategies side by side: conventional monoculture (baseline), regenerative legume rotation, climate-resilient diverse rotation, and agro-ecological forage rotation. For each one it explains why it is suggested, the NASA evidence, benefits, information gaps, risks needing local review, and vulnerability windows. Live daily weather comes from the NASA POWER API, with a calibrated offline fallback model for remote fields. An interactive map shows NASA GIBS layers (MODIS true color, NDVI, land surface temperature, SMAP soil moisture) and four field vulnerability zones: erosion swale, water stress, frost hollow and bare-ground carbon loss. A what-if simulator re-scores rotations for temperature changes of 0 to +4 C and rainfall changes of -40% to +40%, and suggests adaptations such as sowing 12 days earlier. Scoring is transparent and rule-based, not a black-box model. BENEFITS In the app's default case, the legume strategy fixes +58 kg N/ha, saves 28.5% irrigation water and cuts bare fallow from 85 to 18 days. The climate-resilient rotation cuts irrigation by 46.2% in Indus-Ganges and arid regions. Farmers can also add their own crop sequence and enter probe soil moisture or drone NDVI readings. INTENDED IMPACT Heat, erratic rain and falling groundwater threaten farm incomes and food security, but satellite data is hard to use on the farm. FIELDSHIFT AI turns it into clear planning options for water use, soil health and nitrogen, while supporting, not replacing, local farmer expertise, soil tests and extension officer judgment. TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY Flutter and Dart, provider for state management, flutter_map, fl_chart, Firebase Authentication, NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS WMTS tiles, Open-Meteo geocoding and elevation APIs, OpenStreetMap, and GitHub Actions with GitHub Pages for deployment. The app runs on web, Android, iOS and desktop from one codebase. CREATIVITY We combine several NASA datasets (POWER, SMAP, MODIS, GRACE, ECOSTRESS, GPM IMERG, SRTM, HLS) into one workflow, from satellite signal to rotation choice. Simple Farmer and Specialist views, an English, Urdu and Hindi interface, preset farm locations in Pakistan, India, the USA, Kenya and Brazil, CSV export and a printable advisory report make it usable in real farming contexts. FACTORS WE CONSIDERED Gridded data is coarse (about 9 to 50 km), so we state resolution and assumptions openly. Recommendations are heuristics that must be verified locally. We designed for farmers with limited connectivity (offline fallback), different languages, and different irrigation, equipment, soil and market constraints.
